title: CPU and memory efficiency
objective: Spend less CPU time and hold less memory for byte-identical pictures, numbers and digests and the same or better latency, through the changes the owner accepted on 2026-10-03.
context_summary: A read-only audit on 2026-10-03 found the idle path, uploads, subscriptions and the GPU preview's steady state already tight, and the remaining cost in per-pixel kernels (the 16-bit quantizer, spatial tile allocations and batches, Detail and Presence filters, RAW input reads), source preparation (software SHA-256 on aarch64, serial zero-fills, unsized reads), per-tick copying while painting, and build configuration. Owner decisions (docs/decisions.md, CPU and memory efficiency): every byte-identical finding accepted; RAW colour layers stay recomputed per spatial tile; a 64 MiB reduced-grid cache for Clarity and Dehaze; the float mosaic removed through a checked-in librtprocess patch, never by editing vendor/; the catalog in WAL with full flushes; a dist profile with LTO for packaging and timing, deferred by the owner until the timing runs other plans have outstanding are recorded, so this plan measures in release. Every estimate is unmeasured until the final task. The design is docs/design/efficiency.md.

tasks.description: Enable hardware SHA-256 on aarch64, JPEG XL DNG decoding on the shared Rayon pool, and runtime half-float conversion on x86_64.
extra_context: sha2 =0.10.9 compiles its aarch64 SHA-2 backend only with the `asm` feature (sha2-0.10.9/src/sha256.rs cfg_if); the workspace enables no feature and Cargo.lock has no sha2-asm, so every hash on the M4 is software. The aarch64 backend detects the CPU feature at run time (cpufeatures) and falls back to software. Enabling `asm` also pulls in sha2-asm, built with cc, which on x86 replaces only the software fallback. Choose between `features = ["asm"]` with a pinned sha2-asm and a notice, or a pinned sha2 release whose aarch64 backend needs no feature, if one exists and its API change is contained; record which and why in the design.

Consumers that gain: cold source preparation (editor/source.rs prepare_file, source.rs open_source_bytes), artifact verification (artifacts/store.rs), capability hashers, the restoration prefix hash and the analysis identity. Digests are identical; no stored value changes.

jxl-oxide =0.12.6 is declared with default-features = false (crates/luxforge-raw/Cargo.toml), which drops its default `rayon` feature, so JxlThreadPool::none() decodes serially and render_frame cannot be cancelled while it runs. With `rayon`, its default pool is the global Rayon pool, so no private pool is added (rule 9) and no new package enters the lock file. Re-run the Galaxy S22 JPEG XL exactness test.

half is built with default-features = false in luxforge-core and luxforge-ui; on x86_64 without `std` it cannot detect F16C at run time and converts every boundary texel (render/boundary.rs) in software. Enable `std`. aarch64 already uses the hardware conversion at compile time.

tasks.description: Stop scanning every process on the host at launch to report the graphics backend and adapter.
extra_context: crates/luxforge-app/src/app/mod.rs:558 calls iced::system::information(), which (with the workspace's `sysinfo` iced feature) runs System::new_all() and refresh_all() on a spawned thread, walking every process twice, during the startup decode. tasks.description: Read originals with their size, let pooled writers fault in RAW development buffers instead of zero-filling them on one thread, and stop rescanning RAW proxies for non-finite values.
extra_context: crates/luxforge-core/src/source.rs:112 reads through file.take(limit + 1) into Vec::new(); Take hides File's size hint, so the buffer doubles and can hold up to twice the file through the unpack (64 MiB capacity for a 40 MB NEF). Reserve the metadata length (already checked against the limit) with try_reserve_exact before reading, keeping the over-limit refusal.

crates/luxforge-raw zero-fills with Vec::resize on one thread before a pooled pass writes every value: develop.rs:143 (RGB planes, 12 bytes per site; the spec measured a fresh serial 240 MB bzero at 10.8 to 12.5 ms), develop.rs:257 (direct development), lib.rs:810 (u16 mosaic) and dng.rs:1314 (Air 2S warp scratch). Add one fallible zeroed-allocation helper (alloc_zeroed behind a safe wrapper in luxforge-raw, which already permits unsafe, or an equivalent) and use it at each site, so fresh pages are faulted in by the writers as rule 2 asks. Keep the ResourceLimit errors.

crates/luxforge-core/src/proxy.rs:804 builds each RAW proxy through LinearImage::with_fingerprint, which scans every value for finiteness on one thread (source/linear.rs:167). A weighted mean of finite planes is finite; build it through the validated constructor with a debug assertion, and add a test that the proxy of a finite source is accepted without the scan and equals today's planes.
Warm benchmark loops can hide the zero-fill saving because the allocator reuses freed regions; the measurement task measures cold opens.

tasks.description: Replace the 16-bit quantizer's binary search with an exact index that returns the same code for every f32.
extra_context: Implemented as colour::srgb::Quantizer16 (crates/luxforge-core/src/colour.rs, quantizer16()): a 128 KiB index of the square root of [0, 1] in 65,536 bins, no bin holding more than two of the 65,535 thresholds, so a value is compared with at most two. Non-finite values, the signed zeros and the infinities keep the search's answers. Row passes take the index and the 16-bit decode table once rather than per pixel.

Evidence: slow_byte_quantize16_is_the_threshold_search_at_every_f32_in_the_unit_interval compares it with the threshold search at every f32 in [0, 1] and the special values; byte_quantize16_is_monotone_and_exact_at_every_threshold and the byte-domain tests pass unchanged. Its per-value cost and the integrated editor-performance figures are in docs/specs/performance.md; the index is listed in docs/design/architecture.md's limits.

tasks.description: Reuse each batch slot's tile planes instead of allocating fresh zeroed planes for every tile and unit.
extra_context: run_tile (crates/luxforge-core/src/render/spatial.rs:327; the allocations at :368, :377 and :406) does vec![0.0; regions[0].pixels() * 3] for the input and a fresh vec for each unit's output; only TileScratch is reused per slot. At 60 MP with all three Presence fields one tile allocates roughly 125 MB, about 8.8 GB of new zero pages per render; Clarity alone about 46 MB per tile.

Give each batch slot (run_batches keeps one TileScratch per concurrent tile) two plane buffers, ping-ponged between the input and even units and the odd units, grown to the largest request and never cleared. fill and PlanesMut already write every value, the same contract TileScratch documents. tile_output borrows instead of consuming; where a tile's planes must outlive the slot (the RAW frame write-back, the point query's tile cache) copy only the tile rectangle or keep owned buffers for the point path.

Keep the worst-case working set charged to the spatial budget unchanged or smaller (worst_case_working_set). The masked copy fast path (copies_exactly) and the coverage snapshot (cut_out) keep their semantics.

context_links.label: Performance rules
context_links.relevance: Rules and the checklist each change answers.

tasks.description: Replace the barrier between spatial batches with a rolling window under the same budget reservation.
extra_context: run_batches (crates/luxforge-core/src/render/spatial.rs:706) runs a batch of tiles, waits for all of them, then reserves and starts the next. When the spatial target admits a batch as wide as the pool, each tile runs serially on one worker, and on the M4 Pro (10 performance, 4 efficiency cores; the global pool has 14 threads) the batch waits for its slowest tile on an efficiency core. Recorded Presence renders reach about 800 to 1100% of 1400%.

Start a tile as soon as one finishes, within the same reservation and concurrency limit (RenderContext::concurrency), and write tiles back in order. Keep the cancellation check between tiles and the narrow-batch path where each tile's passes run on the pool. Results and their order of arithmetic per value are unchanged.
Do not resize the pool or add a private pool (rule 9).

tasks.description: Read Sharpening's limiter and Detail's reconstruction over row slices in the interior, without per-pixel clamps and assertions.
extra_context: Already done: smoothing, noise reduction's shrinkage (each pixel's chroma energy and factor computed once for a and b) and its level planes run over whole rows, the interior through slices and only the stage-edge columns through the clamped read, with the halo checked once a pass (modules/detail/filters.rs, denoise.rs). modules/detail/exactness.rs holds frozen tap-by-tap references for them.

Add an interior path over row slices for output pixels whose 3 x 3 reach lies inside the held region, with the clamped, asserted path kept for the band near the stage edge so the halo guard still applies there. Each value's own operations and order stay the same. exactness.rs uses Sharpen::limited as its reference; freeze a copy of today's limiter there before changing it.

tasks.description: Read Presence's box, guided and upsample passes over row slices in the interior, interleave independent running sums, and hoist upsample's per-column index and weight.

tasks.description: Read RAW render input by rows instead of per pixel, read portrait planes in blocks, skip per-pixel resolution in segments without replacements, and quantize f32 rows without the f64 guard.
extra_context: load_pulled (crates/luxforge-core/src/render/linear.rs:639) takes its (None, _) arms whenever geometry is not the identity (any exact crop or Orientation layer) or the entry is a spatial frame: per pixel geometry.unmap, entry_pixel, reader.pixel with View::map's orientation match and adjust_source_pixel, or frame_pixel with u64 plane arithmetic. region_in (render/pipeline.rs:715) collects a Vec<[f64; 3]> per row and Linear::colour_row (linear.rs:317) converts f64 to f32 to f64 with a per-pixel finish Result. For a signed-permutation geometry with no entry, compose geometry and view into a first index and stride per row (extend ViewReader::row with an x offset) and copy spans; for a spatial frame entry copy the three plane rows; keep f32 end to end where the value is f32; hoist white_balance.is_none() out of the loop. Keep the per-pixel white-balance overflow error that source_rows_keep_validation_fallback... checks.

ViewReader::row (source/linear.rs:408) walks orientations 5 to 8 with a stride of plus or minus base_width, touching a new row of all three planes per output pixel. Load each chunk as a blocked transpose: walk base rows in order and write the chunk's (up to 16) output rows from each contiguous span.

Segment::resolve (render/compiled.rs:631), called per pixel from pixel_in (pipeline.rs:612), composes ExactGeometry::then for every operation; return straight after unmap when the segment has no pixel replacements (!has_pixels).

The RAW terminal (terminal_srgb, linear.rs:157, and put/write for rows without colour or white balance) widens f32 to f64 and calls Quantizer::rounded with its 1e-12 guard. For an f32 input only a threshold and its next_down can fall in the guard band, which the_f32_thresholds_are_where_both_quantizers_change_code pins; use quantizer.pixel for f32 rows after the non-finite check.
This touches the files the RAW colour-per-tile decision covers; do not add a materialized frame or row-band cache (owner, 2026-10-03).

tasks.description: Reduce the histogram reducer's per-pixel work, stop deep-copying every API answer, prepare the lineage query once, and buffer the live-session writer.
extra_context: Bins::add_pixel (crates/luxforge-core/src/analysis.rs:202) increments r0..b255 per pixel although they equal r[0], r[255] and so on, then clip_class recomputes the same comparisons. Derive the per-channel extremes from the bins when building the report; classify with a 256-entry table e[v] = (v == 0) | (v == 255) << 1, counting e[r] | e[g] | e[b] into a four-way class count for any-channel and e[r] & e[g] & e[b] for all-channel; count in u32 per bounded chunk and widen on merge. It runs between the exact render and the settled frame (preview/worker.rs:417, :761), estimated 5 to 18 ms per settle. Delivering the frame before the report is a separate latency choice, not part of this task.

ApiResponse::success (crates/luxforge-core/src/api/mod.rs:57) calls serde_json::to_value on results that are usually already a Value, rebuilding every answer on the owner thread (largest for asset.state and brush draft.set). Add a constructor that moves a Value in and use it where the answer is one.

history.lineage (crates/luxforge-core/src/editor/history.rs:394) prepares its SELECT on every step of up to 100 after each undo, redo and restore. Use prepare_cached once outside the loop, or one recursive CTE with the same limit and error behaviour.

The TCP session writer (crates/luxforge-core/src/api/transport.rs:138, :200) serializes into a raw TcpStream, one write per JSON fragment, and never sets TCP_NODELAY. Wrap it in a BufWriter flushed at each line and set nodelay. The stdio path is already line-buffered.

tasks.description: Open the catalog in WAL mode with full flushes, so a commit appends once and reaches the drive.
extra_context: EditorService::open (crates/luxforge-core/src/editor.rs:642) sets synchronous=FULL and locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE with the default rollback journal: each commit writes pages twice and syncs three to four times. Bundled SQLite's fullfsync is off by default, so on macOS those syncs are plain fsync and not F_FULLFSYNC, unlike atomic_file::flush, which every other durable write uses.

In the durable build set PRAGMA locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE first, then journal_mode=WAL (so no -shm file is used), synchronous=FULL, fullfsync=ON and checkpoint_fullfsync=ON, and check that journal_mode reports wal. Test builds (test-skip-disk-flush) keep synchronous=OFF and may keep their current journal.

Consequences to cover: the -wal file lives beside the catalog while it is open and after a crash; a clean close checkpoints and removes it; anything that copies or moves a catalog file (search xtask, tests and the desktop for catalog file copies) must include it or close first. The format marker and the explicit refusal of unsupported catalogs are unchanged. Catalog backup stays an open product question.
Update docs/design/versions-and-lineage.md's storage section and docs/design/architecture.md's persistence list to describe the journal and flushing.

tasks.description: Reuse strokes already held by cached entries of the same asset when hydrating a newly read entry.
extra_context: entry_from (crates/luxforge-core/src/editor/catalog.rs:515) calls hydrate_strokes and read_strokes (:378 to :397), which run a SQL lookup, a JSON parse and a SHA-256 check for every referenced stroke. After each commit, undo or redo the next read misses the entry cache and repeats this for strokes the asset's cached entries already hold: O(strokes) per commit and O(n^2) over a painting session (up to 8192 points per mask, 64 strokes per component).

Before querying, resolve stroke IDs from strokes held by cached entries of the same asset (editor/entries.rs), sharing their Arc<dyn StoredStroke>, and query only the rest. Strokes are immutable and content-addressed and those came from the catalog, so the cache's rule that it holds only what the catalog returned still holds. A missing or corrupt stroke still fails explicitly.
acceptance_criteria: Hydrating an entry whose strokes are held by a cached entry of the same asset reads, parses and hashes none of them; a test counts the queries.
A missing or corrupt stroke not held in the cache is still refused; brush history, undo and reopen tests pass.

steps: Run the catalog, entry-cache and mask brush tests.
expected_results: All pass; query counts fall for shared strokes.

tasks.description: Convert the lens warp grid once per held boundary, and copy and compare only the GPU preview blocks whose shared buffer changed.
extra_context: crates/luxforge-app/src/app/gpu_plan.rs (grid.nodes, about line 425) converts the warp grid's nodes (up to 262k, 2 MiB; about 880 KiB at Fit) through a temporary Vec into a new Arc<[u32]> on every tick, reached from gpu_preview.rs:498, although the grid is fixed for the draft. Convert it once when the boundary is held and pass the Arc each tick.

In crates/luxforge-ui/src/photo_surface/gpu_preview.rs, every prepare calls pack, concatenating every program's block into one Vec<u32>; then the slot and each spatial chain link (gpu_preview/chain.rs, write) compare the whole of it with their written_blocks through mask::changed_ranges and copy it again on any difference: 1 to 6 MiB per frame with a warp grid or a heavy brush mask (a brush block can reach GPU_BLOCK_WORDS_MAX = 316,034 words). Program blocks are already Arc<[u32]>: remember each step's (Arc pointer, offset, length), skip copying and comparing blocks whose pointer and offset are unchanged, and process only the steps that changed.
Uploaded words must be identical; the GPU preview's readback qualification and dissolve behaviour are unchanged.
The slot's shared scratch pool (docs/design/gpu-preview.md, Plane sharing and precision) restructures the same chains and slots; keep each link's own schedule.

tasks.description: Build control models only for tool sections that show them, and let export and capability job polls skip the full update when their read changed nothing.
extra_context: section (crates/luxforge-app/src/state/tools.rs:814) builds every section's controls on every message, collapsed or not; the view skips collapsed bodies (view/tools_panel.rs:226) but the derive does not. Control::Presets calls presets_model (state/presets.rs:451), which per preset clones its settings into apply_fields, four to five strings and two lowercase strings, and presettable_groups re-walks every module's control tree: roughly 1 ms per message with a large library, on every drag tick.

Build controls only when SectionModel::shows_controls() would be true. Before gating, find every reader of section control models outside the view (evidence summaries and outcome checks, query_choice.rs, request_visible_curve_samples in app/controls.rs, capabilities::after_derive) and keep each correct, deriving what it needs directly where necessary. Optionally keep a preset row's apply as a flag and build the fields in the handler.

export_poll_subscription and capability_poll_subscription (app/export.rs:330, app/capabilities.rs:429) use time::every(100 ms); each tick yields a Poll then a Read/Polled message, each running every after_message hook, a full derive and a view rebuild. Extend update_inner's fast path (app/mod.rs:620) to a poll read that changed nothing (a non-final export_read, a capability_polled with an equal JobRecord), or wake on job change from the owner as the event waker does. The timer stays gated on a live job.

tasks.description: Remove the normalized float mosaic from RAW development's peak through a checked-in librtprocess patch that reads each site from the u16 mosaic, without editing vendored sources.
extra_context: During development the u16 mosaic (2 bytes per site), the normalized f32 mosaic (4) and the RGB planes (12) coexist: 18 bytes per site, about 1.08 GB at 60 MP, 30 per site while the second development is held. Normalization::run (crates/luxforge-raw/src/normalize.rs) writes ((s - black) * scale) * gain per site; RCD reads it only in its tile fill as LIM01(rawData / 65536) (vendor rcd.cc:124), Markesteijn reads it likewise without a clamp, and border.cc fills the border band from it.

Add crates/luxforge-raw/patches/librtprocess-mosaic.patch, applied by build.rs's apply_patch after librtprocess-local.patch with exact context matching and an allowed-file list, plus its cargo:rerun-if-changed line. Through it rcd.cc, markesteijn.cc and border.cc read each site through one inline function computing the same f32 expression, in the same operations and order, from the u16 mosaic and per-site black, scale and gain tables the adapter passes. No file under vendor/ changes.

Keep today's float-mosaic path for any development whose sensor stage rewrites the float mosaic: DNG sensor-stage corrections (apply_sensor: Pixel 7/8 Pro GainMaps, Leica, Ricoh GR II) and sparse sensor repairs (MAX_CORRECTIONS). Select the path once per development.

Exactness: planes must be bit-identical against the float-mosaic path on every committed Bayer and X-Trans fixture and every RAW-manifest source available on the host, including the Bayer clip at sensor white and X-Trans's unclamped values (bayer_input_clips_at_sensor_white_after_gain_and_x_trans_does_not). Update the luxforge-raw README and THIRD_PARTY notes on local patches, and docs/design/native-demosaic-parallelism.md or initial-raw.md where they describe the peak.

tasks.description: Make a brush tick's cost independent of the stroke's length on the desktop and the owner by building, copying and cloning the points only when they change and are sent.
extra_context: Desktop, per path-growing move: BrushStroke::push (crates/luxforge-app/src/mask_draft/brush.rs:192) drops the memoized decimation; offer_mask (app/masks.rs:1673) calls capture_error, which runs PathCapture::stroke (core path.rs:532, Ramer-Douglas-Peucker over up to 16,384 positions); MaskGesture::fields builds extra_fields (brush.rs:315), cloning points() and json!(points) (one Value per point, up to 1024); app/draft.rs:196 overwrites pending even when a round trip is in flight (draft.rs:287), discarding that work; advance (draft.rs:296) deep-clones the fields into sent; app/gesture.rs:745 clones the set into the session again.

Owner, per tick: api/owner.rs:1483 deep-clones the session including the draft; api/methods.rs:2074 clones the draft; :2083 builds next.request() only to test contains_key; editor/plan.rs:608 builds draft.request() again; the answer repeats the draft.

Fix: build fields only when they will be sent (dirty while in flight, built in advance or on Event::Set); hold decimated points as Arc<[[f64; 2]]> with a cached Value; keep a revision instead of the sent clone; test keys on fields and target directly; snapshot the session only for handlers that can park a pixel read, or share the draft behind an Arc; avoid the second request(). The wire protocol is unchanged; append-only points are an API change outside this task.
Frozen coverage, draft identities, evidence semantics (frame_pending, drained) and one entry per stroke are unchanged.

tasks.description: Add the reduced-grid cache for Clarity's and Dehaze's stage-anchored reductions under rule 14, and read tiles and point samples from it.
extra_context: Clarity's encoded-luminance 4x block grid (crates/luxforge-core/src/modules/presence/clarity.rs:142) and Dehaze's reduced grid (dehaze.rs:262) are anchored at the stage origin and independent of the tile and of the unit's amount, but every tile rebuilds them over its halo: about 2.7x the stage in encodes for Clarity at 60 MP, and again on every amount change. Owner decision 2026-10-03: cache them.

Contract (rule 14): the value is the f32 reduced plane a unit builds before applying any coefficient; a unit declares that it has one, beside SpatialUnit::estimate_key. The key mirrors EstimateKey (render/context.rs:336): source fingerprint and development identity, the prefix hash of the layers before the operation, stage dimensions and the phase's sampling (exact, proxy or window), and the unit's own reduction key; not its position or amount. One store in RenderContext beside EstimateStore, 64 MiB in total, named in docs/design/architecture.md's limits; evict least recently used before adding past the budget; refuse to hold an entry larger than the budget.

Fill on the shared pool as its own pass before the operation's tiles in the render that first needs it, never on the owner or interface thread, cancelled with the render. Tiles read sub-rectangles; the guided filter stays per tile; when the plane covers the reach, shrink the tile's fill to what other units' halos still need. A point sample reads the plane when present and otherwise computes its window as today; both give the same byte.

Tests: a hit returns the bytes a recomputation gives; each key part, changed alone, misses; the budget evicts and refuses; a render with and without the cache is byte-identical in both domains; a sample equals the rendered byte with and without the cached plane. Record hit rate across an amount drag and settle, rebuild cost and retained bytes in the measurement task.

Each masked Presence layer reads its own input, so each has its own entry, and at 60 MP 64 MiB holds about one Dehaze entry. A recipe may hold 16 masked spatial layers (docs/decisions.md, GPU previews), so include a stack of several masked Clarity and Dehaze layers at 60 MP in the adoption measurement and report its hit rate across an amount drag after a settle.

tasks.description: Measure the finished efficiency work against its base on the M4 and record what each change saved, reverting any change that does not pay for itself.
extra_context: Timing waits for every feature task (rule 13). Build the base commit and the integrated branch, both in the release profile (the dist profile is deferred), back to back; run each workload alternately base/branch and reversed, on a quiet host, recording load, host, profile and cache state.

Workloads: editor-performance on the generated 24 MP and 60 MP JPEGs (Basic then Presence, Detail, Presence after Detail, masked stacks); cold open and committed white balance for each RAW-manifest source with peak RSS and the development's peak; editor-latency drag, paint (long stroke) and settle at 24 and 60 MP, and --presence and --detail drags; a Clarity amount drag for the reduced-grid cache's hit rate, rebuild cost and retained bytes; measure for launch and idle; commit latency with the WAL catalog.

Where the desktop and owner tasks' savings show: the launch scan is skipped only in a normal launch, so measure's empty, 24mp and 60mp workloads (evidence launches) still ask for system information and only its idle row is a normal launch; a brush tick's owner copies are counted by tests/draft_tick (one copy of the path on an unplanned tick, three over a spatial stack) and its latency by editor-latency --mode paint; a collapsed section's saving is per message, largest with a large preset library; the WAL catalog's is commit latency (an import, a slider commit and a stroke commit).

Record results in docs/specs/performance.md under a section of their own, update docs/engineering/performance-rules.md (anti-patterns removed: the serial zero-fills and per-tile planes), docs/features.md and the design's status. A change whose measured saving is nil or negative on its own workload is reverted and recorded as tried.
